_comment_search_backend: Where web results come from. Use 'ddgs' for a zero-infrastructure Python or PyPI install, 'searxng' for the bundled Docker stack, 'duckduckgo' to force that DDGS backend, or 'auto' to try SearXNG then fall back.
_comment_search_backend_url: SearXNG's JSON search endpoint. This Docker hostname works inside compose.yaml; use your reachable HTTP URL outside Docker.
_comment_search_backend_fallback: When true, fall back to DDGS if the selected SearXNG backend fails. Keep this enabled unless searches must stay inside your SearXNG instance.
_comment_search_engines: Optional SearXNG engine names. Leave empty to use the engines enabled by the SearXNG instance.
_comment_search_region: Optional regional search code such as 'us-en'. Leave empty for backend defaults.
_comment_searxng_timeout_seconds: Timeout for TinySearch's request to SearXNG. This is separate from SearXNG's own per-engine timeouts.
_comment_ddgs_backend: DDGS text-search backend selection. 'auto' lets DDGS choose; set a supported DDGS backend name only when you need to pin one.
_comment_ddgs_timeout_seconds: Timeout for one DDGS request. Increase this on slow networks; reduce it when fast failure is preferable.
_comment_search_max_results: Search only. Number of backend-ordered discovery results returned by the MCP search tool.
_comment_search_max_concurrent_items: Maximum independent search items run at once in one batch.
_comment_scrape_max_tokens: Scrape tools only. Maximum content tokens returned for each MCP scrape_url or scrape_urls item.
_comment_scrape_max_links: Maximum related-link navigation candidates returned per page. Set to zero to skip link extraction and ranking.
_comment_scrape_max_link_tokens: Separate total token budget for related-link navigation candidates; it never reduces evidence tokens.
_comment_search_top_k: Deprecated, unused by any shipped pipeline (formerly the removed research tool). Number of raw search results requested before reranking.
_comment_chunk_rrf_cutoff: Scrape. Minimum reciprocal-rank-fusion score for page chunks. Zero disables score filtering.
_comment_chunk_dense_weight: Scrape. Dense-vector share of chunk ranking from 0 to 1; BM25 receives the remaining share. Dense ranking is required, so do not set this to zero.
_comment_pipeline_timeout_seconds: Overall per-page fetch timeout in seconds, used by scrape. Use null to disable the timeout.
_comment_crawl_fit_markdown_mode: How Crawl4AI selects relevant markdown: 'bm25', 'pruning', or 'none'. BM25 is query-aware; pruning is query-independent.
_comment_crawl_fit_min_chars: Use the fitted markdown only when it contains at least this many characters, avoiding nearly empty filtered pages.
_comment_crawl_bm25_threshold: Crawl4AI BM25 content-filter threshold used when crawl_fit_markdown_mode is 'bm25'.
_comment_crawl_bm25_language: Language used by Crawl4AI's BM25 filter.
_comment_crawl_pruning_threshold: Crawl4AI pruning threshold used when crawl_fit_markdown_mode is 'pruning'.
_comment_crawl_max_chunk_tokens: Target maximum tokens in each candidate page chunk before reranking.
_comment_crawl_overlap_tokens: Tokens repeated between adjacent chunks to preserve context across boundaries.
_comment_crawl_max_page_tokens: Maximum tokens retained from one crawled page before chunking. Zero disables the per-page limit.
_comment_browser_backend: Browser automation backend for the browser_* tools. 'playwright' drives the same Chromium the scraper already installs; 'off' removes the tools entirely.
_comment_browser_cdp_url: Optional external Chrome DevTools Protocol endpoint, used by both scraping and the browser tools. Leave empty to launch a local Chromium. Keep remote CDP endpoints private and authenticated.
_comment_browser_storage_state_path: Optional Playwright storage-state JSON file holding cookies and local storage. Sessions are isolated and seed from this file, so a cookie or consent banner is accepted once rather than on every navigation. Server-side only: never exposed to a model or over HTTP.
_comment_browser_snapshot_depth: Default maximum accessibility-tree depth per snapshot. A smaller depth returns a shallower but still valid tree and costs far fewer tokens. Zero means unlimited.
_comment_browser_response_char_budget: Maximum characters returned from one browser tool call before truncation. Zero disables capping.
_comment_browser_idle_shutdown_seconds: Close a warm scraper or interactive browser session after this many idle seconds.
_comment_browser_action_timeout_seconds: Default per-action deadline for clicks, typing, and waits.
_comment_embedding_backend: Embedding implementation. Use 'onnx' for private local CPU embeddings or 'openai_compatible' for an OpenAI-compatible embedding API.
_comment_embedding_model: For ONNX, choose 'fast', 'balanced', 'quality', or a Hugging Face ONNX repository id. Ignored by the openai_compatible backend, whose model comes from its env file.
_comment_embedding_openai_env_file: Path to the env file containing OPENAI_API_KEY, optional OPENAI_BASE_URL, and OPENAI_EMBEDDING_MODEL. Used only by openai_compatible embeddings.
_comment_max_concurrent_embedding_calls: Maximum embedding batches in flight. Raise for a remote API with available quota; lower for rate limits or constrained local CPU.
_comment_embedding_timeout_seconds: Timeout for one embedding call or batch.
_comment_embedding_timeout_retries: Number of retries after an embedding timeout.
_comment_dense_document_embed_batch_size: Number of documents sent through the dense embedder per batch. Lower it to reduce peak memory.
_comment_dense_query_prefix: Instruction prepended before embedding a query. The bundled Compose profile leaves it empty for the default MiniLM model; use model-specific instructions when required.
_comment_dense_document_prefix: Instruction prepended before embedding each result or chunk. Leave empty unless the selected embedding model requires one.
_comment_encoding_name: Tokenizer used for token budgets. Use 'embedding' to match the selected embedding model, or a tiktoken encoding such as 'o200k_base'.
_comment_blocked_domains: Domains TinySearch must neither return nor crawl. A domain entry also blocks its subdomains.
